Electronics: diode and transistor models for amplifiers, switches, and logic gates. Multiple transistor circuit analysis, op amps, and electronic systems.
Prereq: Engr 1182, and ECE 2100 or 2020; or 2021 or 2106, and 2027. Prereq or concur: ECE or EngPhys major; or 2110 and permission of department.
courses.prereq: Engr 1182, and ECE 2100 or 2020; or 2021 or 2106, and 2027

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Electronics Laboratory
courses.description:
Electronic amplification, signal processing, timing, and power regulation circuits. Experiments with electronics evaluation modules and use of an analog system lab kit for electronics testing.
Prereq: 3020; and ECE or EngPhysics major.
courses.prereq: 3020; and ECE or EngPhysics major

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Electronic Devices
courses.description:
Semiconductor materials and devices. Crystals; bandstructure; charge carrier statistics; excess carriers, transport; PN junction; Schottky barrier; bipolar and field-effect transistors; optoelectronic devices.
Prereq: Physics 1251, 1261, or both 1240 and 1241; and Chem 1210, 1220, or 1250; and enrollment in ECE, MSE, or EngPhysics major. Prereq or concur: Math 2415 or 2174.
courses.prereq: Physics 1251, 1261, or both 1240 and 1241; and Chem 1210, 1220, or 1250; and enrollment in ECE, MSE, or EngPhysics major

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Sustainable Energy and Power Systems I
courses.description:
Introduction to electrical energy systems: history, current trends, renewable and non-renewable sources, rotating machines and their operation, and smart grid initiatives.
Prereq: 2100, 2100.02, 2105, 2020, 2021, 205, 292, or 294 (Spring 2011), and enrollment in ECE or EngPhysics major. Not open to students with credit for 341.
courses.prereq: 2100, 2100.02, 2105, 2020, 2021, 205, 292, or 294 (Spring 2011), and enrollment in ECE or EngPhysics major

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Sustainable Energy and Energy Conversion Lab
courses.description:
Laboratory introducing basics of energy conversion processes for electrical energy supply systems utilizing conventional rotating machines and hardware-in-the-loop simulation system for sustainable energy systems.
Prereq: 3040, and enrollment in ECE or EngPhysics major.
courses.prereq: 3040, and enrollment in ECE or EngPhysics major

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Signals and Systems
courses.description:
Linear systems and models in continuous and discrete time; convolution; Fourier series and transform; frequency response; Laplace transform; z-transform; applications.
Prereq: 2020, 2050, and 2060; or 2100; and Math 2174 or 2568; and enrollment in ECE or EngPhysics major.
courses.prereq: 2020, 2050, and 2060; or 2100; and Math 2174 or 2568; and enrollment in ECE or EngPhysics major

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Feedback Control Systems
courses.description:
Provides fundamental concepts in feedback control systems design and analysis.
Prereq: 3050.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced Digital Design
courses.description:
Design and analysis of sequential circuits; digital circuit design using building blocks, programmable logic devices; design of basic computer components such as arithmetic logic units.
Prereq: 2000, 2060, 2061, 2010, 2000.02, 290, 294 (Autumn 2010) or 206 and 261. Prereq or concur: 3020 (323), and enrollment in ECE, EngPhys, or CSE majors; or prereq  or concur 2010  and permission of department. Not open to students with credit for 561.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Microcontroller Lab
courses.description:
Laboratory in which a microcontroller is used to interface real-world hardware to make a functioning system.
Prereq: 2560 or CSE 2421, and enrollment in ECE, CSE, or EngPhysics major. Not open to students with credit for 3567.01.
courses.prereq: 2560 or CSE 2421, and enrollment in ECE, CSE, or EngPhysics major

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Capstone Design I
courses.description:
Fundamentals of the engineering design process. Application of design principles and methodology to conceptual and detailed technical design. Technical writing and communications skills. Project management during design.
Prereq or Concur: 3080 or Philos 1332; and ECE 2560, 3010, 3020, 3027, 3030, 3040, and 3050; and GE Writing/Comm level 2 or Writing and Info Lit; and GenEd 1201 or 2601; and Sr standing; and enrollment in Electrical Eng Program of Study (EES subplan). Prereq or concur - Option 2: 2050 or 2100, and 3080 or Philos 1332, and ECE 3020, 3027, 3561, 3567, CSE 2231, and 2451, and GenEd 1201 or 2601, and Sr standing, and enrollment in Computer Eng Program or Study (CES subplan). Not open to students with credit for 3900, 3905, 4900, 4900H, 4901, or Engr 5901.01.This course is progress graded.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Analog Integrated Circuits I
courses.description:
Fundamentals of analog integrated circuits. CMOS transistors and diodes large-signal and small-signal operation and modeling. On-chip passive components operation and modeling. Simple and advanced current mirrors, single-ended and differential CMOS amplifiers, CMOS OTAs and Op-Amps. Integrated Circuits Fabrication, Packaging, and Testing.
Prereq: 3020. Not open to students with credit for 5021.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Individual Studies in Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.description: Individual studies project. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 12 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Automotive Manufacturing
courses.description:
This course is an introduction to automotive manufacturing as implemented in the certificate program at OSU in the College of Engineering.
Prereq: Engr 1181.xx and 1182.xx, or 1281.xx and 1282.xx, or 1186.xx and 1187 and 1188; and enrollment in the College of Engineering. Not open to students with credit for WeldEng 4610, ISE 4610 or MechEng 4610. Cross-listed in WeldEng 4610, ISE 4610 and MechEng 4610.
courses.prereq: Engr 1181.xx and 1182.xx, or 1281.xx and 1282.xx, or 1186.xx and 1187 and 1188; and enrollment in the College of Engineering

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Capstone Design II
courses.description:
Application of project management, design principles and methodology to conceptual and detailed technical design, implementation, and testing of a capstone project.
Prereq: 3905 and 3090, or 3906. Not open to students with credit for 4900, 4900H, 4901, Engr 5901.01, 5901.02H, 5902.01, or 5902.02H.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Capstone Design II with Honors Thesis
courses.description:
Application of design principles and methodology to conceptual and detailed technical design, implementation and testing, culminating in a capstone design project.
Prereq: Honors standing; and 3905 and 3090, or 3906; and permission of department. Not open to students with credit for 4900, 4900H, 4901, Engr 5902.01 or 5902.01H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing; and 3905 and 3090, or 3906; and permission of department

courses.title: Undergraduate Honors Research

courses.description: Undergraduate Thesis (Distinction) research on topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering. Prereq: GPA 3.0 or above, and enrollment in ECE major, and approved Thesis (Distinction) project. Repeatable to a maximum of 6 cr hrs or 6 completions.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Analog and Digital Communications
courses.description:
Communications channel modeling, analog communication schemes, digital communication schemes, error rate analysis, and error control coding.
Prereq: 3050, and Stat 3470 or Physics 3700; or Grad standing.
courses.prereq: 3050, and Stat 3470 or Physics 3700; or Grad standing

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Antennas
courses.description: Electromagnetic radiation; fundamental antenna parameters; dipole, loops, patches, broadband and other antennas; array theory; ground plane effects; horn and reflector antennas; pattern synthesis; antenna measurements. Prereq: 3010 (312), or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences. Not open to students with credit for 711.
courses.prereq: 3010 (312), or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Integrated Optics
courses.description:
Fundamentals of planar lightwave circuits and guided wave devices; laser light in anisotropic media; electrooptic and nonlinear optical effects; concepts in telecommunications, RF photonics, nanobiotechnology.
Prereq: 3010, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 3010, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Microwave Engineering
courses.description:
Transmission line theory; multiconductor; S-parameters; transformers, couplers, filters, resonators, circulators; electromagnetic interference and compatibility; computer-aided design; microstrip realization and testing with a network analyzer.
Prereq: 3010, and enrollment in ECE major; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 3010, and enrollment in ECE major; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Mixed Signal VLSI
courses.description:
Design and circuit analysis of basic VLSI structures such as registers, cell libraries, digital and analog I/O. Physical layout, timing analysis, PLLs, design tools.
Prereq: 3020, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 3020, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to RF Systems
courses.description:
Intuitive system design methods to dissect the radio modem in analog & digital domains with emphasis on: a) performance evaluation using hand calculations and simulation, and b) understanding of the interaction between RF components and radio architectures. Topics include: system parameters, propagation & antennas, noise, distortion, modulation & aerial access, phase noise, RF transceivers.
Prereq or concur: 4021 or 5021, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Power Electronics: Devices, Circuits, and Applications
courses.description: Provides an introduction to power electronic conversion principles. Analytical techniques will be developed through the study of widely used converter circuits. Prereq: 3020 (323), or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences. Not open to students with credit for 624, 724, or 844.
courses.prereq: 3020 (323), or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Microwave Electronics
courses.description: Design principles of microwave transistor amplifiers and oscillators; low-noise, power and broadband amplifiers; linearization; computer-aided design; microstrip realizations and testing in the laboratory. Prereq: 3020 (323), and enrollment in ECE major; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Science, or Math and Physical Sciences. Not open to students with credit for 723.
courses.prereq: 3020 (323), and enrollment in ECE major; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Science, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Process Technology
courses.description:
Discrete and integrated circuit device design, silicon VLSI processing technologies, III-V compound semiconductor device fabrication technologies; epitaxy, doping, bandgap engineering; and device measurements and failure mechanisms.
Prereq: 3030, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 3030, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Solid State Electronics and Photonics Laboratory
courses.description:
Introduction to Introduction to laboratory techniques for semiconductor device fabrication including photolithography, oxidation, diffusion, chemical processes, reactive ion etching, and metallization; fabrication and measurements of visible light emitting diodes (LED) and GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT).
Prereq: 3030 or MatScEn 3271; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 3030 or MatScEn 3271; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Electric Machines
courses.description: Principles of electromechanical energy conversion; basic structures of electric machines; steady state models and performance analysis; advanced topics on AC machine control. Prereq: 3020 (323) and 3040 (341), or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences. Not open to students with credit for 743.
courses.prereq: 3020 (323) and 3040 (341), or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Power Systems
courses.description:
A power system analysis course presenting power systems loads, modeling of transformers and power system model for voltage calculation and faults.
Prereq: 3040, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 3040, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Wireless Networking
courses.description:
Fundamental concepts in cellular design, Wireless-LANs, MANETs, and sensor networks will be explored. Specific topics will include propagation, fading, cellular-design, power-management, routing, scheduling, and control.
Undergrad Prereq: 3561 or CSE 3461, and Stat 2450 or 3470.xx. Grad Prereq: Grad standing in Engineering or Math and Physical Sciences. Not open to students with credit for CSE 5463. Cross-listed in CSE 5463.
courses.prereq: 3561 or CSE 3461, and Stat 2450 or 3470.xx

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Power Electronics Lab
courses.description: Laboratory introducing basic circuits of power electronics, and simulation and control hardware and software for various power and energy applications. Prereq: 3040 (341) and enrollment in ECE major, or Grad standing in Engineering. Not open to students with credit for 628 or 647.
courses.prereq: 3040 (341) and enrollment in ECE major, or Grad standing in Engineering

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Photonics
courses.description:
Fiber optics, optical systems and devices, optical detection, photonic band gaps, holography, and optical data storage.
Prereq: 3010, 3010.01, or 3010.02, and 3030 or 3030.01; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences. Not open to students with credit for 5132.01.
courses.prereq: 3010, 3010.01, or 3010.02, and 3030 or 3030.01; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Signal Processing
courses.description:
Sampling and reconstruction; discrete-time rate conversion; processing of discrete-time signals; design of discrete-time filters, selected topics in adaptive filtering, time-frequency analysis, and wavelets.
Prereq: 3050, and Stat 3470 or Math 4530; or Grad standing.
courses.prereq: 3050, and Stat 3470 or Math 4530; or Grad standing

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Si and Wide Band Gap Power Devices
courses.description:
Basic design and operation of Si and Wide Band Gap (WBG: SiC, GaN and ultra wide band gap semiconductors) power devices and the applications of commercial devices in power electronics applications. Trade-offs between various devices. Static and dynamic operation. Comparison of Si and SiC devices and design differences.
Prereq: 3030, or MatScEn 3271; or Grad standing in Engr or Physics. Not open to students with credit for 5194.07 or 5234.
courses.prereq: 3030, or MatScEn 3271; or Grad standing in Engr or Physics

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning for ECE
courses.description:
Introduction to Machine Learning. Coverage includes linear regression, linear classification, model and feature selection, neural networks, clustering, and principle components analysis. Python will be used for implementation examples.
Prereq: CSE 1222 or Engr 1281.xx; and Math 2568 and Stat 3470; and enrollment in ECE major; or Grad standing in ECE. Not open to students with credit for 4194.02 (Sp19, Machine Learning), 4300, 5300, or MechEng 5194 (Au19, Applied ML for MAE).
courses.prereq: CSE 1222 or Engr 1281.xx; and Math 2568 and Stat 3470; and enrollment in ECE major; or Grad standing in ECE

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Computer Architecture and Design
courses.description:
Design of general purpose digital computers including arithmetic and control units, input/output, and memory subsystems.
Prereq: 2560 and 3561, and undergraduate enrollment in ECE, CSE, or EngPhysics major; or Grad standing in Engineering. Not open to students with credit for CSE 3421.
courses.prereq: 2560 and 3561, and undergraduate enrollment in ECE, CSE, or EngPhysics major; or Grad standing in Engineering

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Instrumentation, Signals, and Control in Transportation Applications
courses.description:
Interdisciplinary course bringing together electrical engineering tools and transportation applications. Students gain valuable experience working in teams while learning traffic flow, surveillance and control.
Prereq: 2020 and 2050, and Math 2415; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for CivilEn 4750 or 6750. Cross-listed in CivilEn 5750.
courses.prereq: 2020 and 2050, and Math 2415; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Image Processing
courses.description:
Fundamentals and research directions in image processing: cameras, geometry, calibration, 2D and 3D image reconstruction, stereo, structure from motion, Radiometry, filtering, motion estimation, and applications.
Prereq: Stat 3470, and Math 2568; or Grad standing in Engr, BioSci, Stat, BioMinf, or PhysSci.
courses.prereq: Stat 3470, and Math 2568; or Grad standing in Engr, BioSci, Stat, BioMinf, or PhysSci

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Real Time Robotics Systems
courses.description:
Components of a robot system, robot forward and reverse kinematics; robot dynamics; robot force generation, robot trajectory generation.
Prereq: Math 2177 or 2174, or 2415 and 2568; and Physics 1250, 1250H, 1260, or 2300; and CSE 1221, 1222, Engr 1181, 1281.01H, 1281.02H, 1221, or 1222; or Grad standing in Engr; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for MechEng 5463 or 7752. Cross-listed in MechEng.
courses.prereq: Math 2177 or 2174, or 2415 and 2568; and Physics 1250, 1250H, 1260, or 2300; and CSE 1221, 1222, Engr 1181, 1281.01H, 1281.02H, 1221, or 1222; or Grad standing in Engr; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Nonlinear and Dynamic Programming for ECE
courses.description:
Introduction to Optimization, including unconstrained optimization, gradient descent, Newton?s method, convexity, constrained optimization, KKT, duality, dynamic programming, basic reinforcement learning, and applications of optimization in ECE.
Prereq: Math 2568 and 2415; or Grad standing in Engineering or Math and Physical Sciences. Not open to students with credit for 5759.
courses.prereq: Math 2568 and 2415; or Grad standing in Engineering or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Semiconductors for Microelectronics and Photonics
courses.description:
Crystal structure, semiconductor energy band structure, electron transport and carrier recombination, heterostructures, and optical and dielectric properties.
Prereq: 3030, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 3030, or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: State-Space Control Systems
courses.description:
Discrete-time state variable representations; pole placement via state-feedback; introduction to realization theory; observer design; introduction to Kalman filtering; linear quadratic regulator theory.
Prereq or concur: 3551; or Graduate standing in Engineering, Math, or Physical Sciences; or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Autonomy in Vehicles
courses.description:
First course on automated driving vehicles and their sub-systems; automated driving history and architectures; car following control; steering control for path tracking, lane keeping; collision mitigation and avoidance; localization and situational awareness; lower and higher-level decision making including deep learning; connected vehicle technologies; evaluation of autonomous driving function.
Prereq: 3551, 5551, or Grad standing in Engineering.
courses.prereq: 3551, 5551, or Grad standing in Engineering

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Applied Control Systems
courses.description:
Application of digital control system theory, from viewpoints of input-output and state variable representations, to realistic problems in automotive powertrain systems.
Prereq: 5551; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences.
courses.prereq: 5551; or Grad standing in Engineering, Biological Sciences, or Math and Physical Sciences

courses.title: Fundamentals of Engineering for Honors I

courses.description:

Prereq: Physics 1250, or 1250H. Prereq or concur: Math 2177, or 2174.

courses.description: Applications of soil and water processes in agricultural and ecological engineering, including: precipitation, infiltration, runoff, hydrographs, water quality, and geospatial analysis of natural resource problems.

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: Thermodynamics in Food, Agricultural and Biological Engineering
courses.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics applied to food, agricultural, biological, and ecological systems. Prereq or concur: Math 2177, 2255, 2415 or 2174. Not open to students with credit for ChBE 508 and 509, or MechEng 501.

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: Heat and Mass Transfer in Food, Agricultural and Biological Engineering
courses.description:

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: System Dynamics and Electricity
courses.description: Modeling of mechanical, fluid, thermal, electrical, and bio-systems. Analytical, computer simulation and experimental solution methods. 1st and 2nd order systems, frequency response. Electric power distribution, electric motor selection and control. Prereq: Physics 1251 (132), and Math 2174 (415), 2177 (415), 2415 (415), or 2255 (255). Not open to students with credit for 425.

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: Cultivating Communities: Engineering for Food Security and Urban Sustainability
courses.description: This course examines the intersection of engineering, food security, urban sustainability, and the role of community organizations in addressing local challenges. Through lectures, readings, discussions, field visits, and group projects, students will apply engineering design principles to develop solutions for small-scale farms and urban agriculture in collaboration with community partners.

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: Introduction to Humanitarian Engineering
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the field of Humanitarian Engineering, cover a variety of potential career paths in this field, explore engineering equations as they apply to problem solving in low-resource settings, introduce students to reflection and communication skills for working as engineers in sustainable development and discuss cultural constraints for engineering problems.

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: Introduction to Humanitarian Engineering Laboratory
courses.description:
This course will introduce students to the field of Humanitarian and Development Innovation through experience-based learning. Weekly experiential activities will build context for engineering design and technologies to enhance sustainability in low resource settings as development workers. The overarching goal is to understand limits to human existence that inform humanitarian engineering design.
Concur: 3210.

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: Sustainability of the Food Supply Chain
courses.description:
Sustainability of the food supply chain depends on the efficiency of transforming raw food materials into consumer food products. This course introduces key operations in each sector of the supply chain along with sustainability parameters, focusing on energy, water, and waste. Students will recognize the challenges of maintaining a sustainable food supply while minimizing environmental impact.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for AgSysMt 3400, FdScTe 3400, or FdScTe 3400.01. Cross-listed in FdScTe.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for AgSysMt 3400, FdScTe 3400, or FdScTe 3400.01

courses.title: Fundamentals of Food and Biological Engineering Processes
courses.description:

Prereq: Math 1172.

courses.subject: FABENG
courses.title: Unit Operations in Food Engineering
courses.description:
Study of unit operations in preserving foods by thermal and alternative food processing methods through problem solving and experimentation. Interdependence of food engineering, chemistry, and microbiology principles in food preservation.
Prereq: 3120 and Micrbio 4000 (Micrbiol 509) or equiv, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 584 or FdScTe 5400 (630). Cross-listed in FdScTe 5400.

courses.subject: ISE
courses.title: Engineering Economics In-Person
courses.description:
Economic analysis of engineering project alternatives. Cash flow modeling; time value of money; techniques for comparing project alternatives and making solid business recommendations; influence of financial accounting and cost accounting on cash flow models. Course uses MS Excel as primary business tool for modeling.
Prereq: Soph, Jr, or Senior standing in Engineering or BSET program.

courses.subject: ISE
courses.title: Design of Work: Methods and Measurement
courses.description:
Introduces students to tools and techniques used in work methods design and productivity improvement, including operation analysis, motion study, value engineering, predetermined time systems, time study, line balancing.
Prereq: Soph standing; and enrollment in Industrial and Systems Engineering major or Engineering Physics major. Additional prereq for students enrolled in ISE major: a grade of C- or above in Stat 3470.01 or 3470.02.

courses.subject: ISE
courses.title: Introduction to Manufacturing Engineering
courses.description: Fundamentals of common manufacturing processes, materials and tooling; relationship of product design to required processing sequences and steps, attributes of manufacturing systems. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 350 or IndEng 311.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 350 or IndEng 311

courses.title: Linear and Integer Programming
courses.description:
Introduction to formulation, solution and analysis of continuous and discrete linear models to optimize the design of production and service systems and other engineering applications.
Prereq: C- or above in Math 2568 or 2174; and CSE 1224, or 2221, or Engr 1281.01H or 1281.02H; and enrollment in ISE or Engineering Physics major. Additional prereq or concur for students enrolled in ISE major: ISE 2400 and CSE 2112.
courses.prereq: C- or above in Math 2568 or 2174; and CSE 1224, or 2221, or Engr 1281.01H or 1281.02H; and enrollment in ISE or Engineering Physics major

courses.description:
Introduction to production systems control: deterministic and stochastic, static and dynamic, single-stage and multi-stage inventory control, MRP systems, just-in-time, scheduling. Facility and machine location models, storage models (warehouse, ASRS), simple layout models, systematic layout planning with applications in manufacturing, health care, service and logistics.

courses.subject: ISE
courses.title: Cognitive Engineering Systems

Human-centered design of cognitive tools and work systems. Human-computer interaction; decision making; human error; computer-supported distributed work; design of decision support systems.

courses.prereq: 2400, and enrollment in ISE major; or enrollment in Engineering Physics major

courses.subject: ISE
courses.title: Engineering Project Management
courses.description:

courses.description:
The Knowlton Landscape Co-Op Program provides students the opportunity to gain valuable professional work experience. The program is open to students in the third year of the BSLA program and allows students to earn credit for an advanced design studio (6 credits) in the spring semester. Interested students must apply and be selected in the autumn term of their UG3 year. To apply, students prepare submission materials which include a portfolio, resume, and cover letters. Students participate in a series of online Meet and Greets to familiarize themselves with the participating firms. Firms then select students to interview from their application pools. Students and firms are matched based on a ranked preferences provided by both parties. Once offers are given and students accept, they coordinate to for the spring term. Selected students work full-time in a firm during the spring of their UG3 year. This gives students hands-on experience with real landscape architecture projects and
Prereq: 2920, 2930 and 3940.

The Co-Op Seminar provides Knowlton Landscape Co-Op students an integrated seminar in which students retain contact with the Knowlton School and other Co-Op students during their Co-Op. While the Co-Op Studio focuses on the work of the firm, the seminar focuses on the Co-Op cohort. This seminar asks students to reflect on their Co Op experience, creating resources of structure and support while the students are away from campus that can be shared with their peers and future Co Op students. Students provide weekly blog posts and participate in discussion groups responding to questions posed by the instructor. During their time at Co-Op students will also contribute to a Field Guide. A living document shared year to year between cohorts to provide resources, tips, and other transferable lessons from working in a firm. Lastly, the students will prepare short videos of them in the field, on site visits, and spending time with their firm.

Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 12 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Individual Studies in Materials Science & Engineering
courses.description: Investigations in areas of advanced non-thesis research. Library and/or research investigations under the directions of instructors. Comprehensive report required. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 12 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Advanced Metals Laboratory
courses.description: Advanced laboratory covering various topics in metallic materials. Prereq: 2241, 2331, 3141, 3261, and 3332. Prereq or concur: 5441 or 5451; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 669, or to Grad students enrolled in MatScEn or WeldEng.

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Physical Metallurgy
courses.description: Physical metallurgy of ferrous and non-ferrous alloys. Emphasis on alloy design, processing and structure-property relations. Prereq: 3141, 3261, and enrollment as MatScEn-BS major student; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for both 661 and 663.
courses.prereq: 3141, 3261, and enrollment as MatScEn-BS major student; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Ceramics Processing Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory experiments involving synthesis/fabrication and characterization of high performance technical ceramics. Prereq: 3141, 3261, 3271, 3332, and enrollment as MatScEn-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 619.
courses.prereq: 3141, 3261, 3271, 3332, and enrollment as MatScEn-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Electronic, Optical, and Magnetic Properties Laboratory
courses.description:
The course will focus on correlation of electronic and optical properties of materials with the material type, structure, composition, and microstructure.
Prereq: 2010, 2241, or 3271, or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2010, 2241, or 3271, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Ceramic Processing
courses.description: Overview of ceramics processing, including essential topics of: powder synthesis/characterization, colloidal/sol-gel processing, shaping/consolidation, sintering, microstructure development and nanoceramics, and thin films/coating. Prereq: 3141, 3151, and enrollment as MatScEn-BS major; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 615.
courses.prereq: 3141, 3151, and enrollment as MatScEn-BS major; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Electroceramics II: Dielectric, Magnetic, and Optical Ceramics
courses.description:
Dielectric, Magnetic, and Optical Ceramics and their applications in devices. Emphasis on the processing-microstructure-property correlation.
Prereq: 3271, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 5571.
courses.prereq: 3271, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Ultrafast Laser Materials Processing
courses.description:
Students are expected to learn basics of laser, non-linear optics, ultrafast lasers, how intense ultrafast lasers interact with materials and ultrafast laser materials processing with a mathematical framework and hands on experience on how an ultrafast laser works, laser safety and how to characterize it and use it to modify materials.
Prereq: Math 1150, 1172, and Physics 1250 or equivalent. Prereq or concur: Physics 1251 or equivalent.
courses.prereq: Math 1150, 1172, and Physics 1250 or equivalent

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Materials in Medicine
courses.description: The materials science of plastics, metals and ceramics currently used to replace or supplement tissues within the human body. Prereq: 2010 and 3611; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for both 645 and 646.
courses.prereq: 2010 and 3611; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Biomaterials Laboratory
courses.description: A laboratory experience in the processing and characterization of biomaterials used for the replacement of human tissues. Prereq or concur: 5611 or 5641; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 649.

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Structure-Property Relationships of Polymers
courses.description: An understanding of the structure/property relationships that drive the continued expansion of polymers into a wide array of applications. Prereq: 2010, CPHR 2.0 or higher, and rank 3 or 4 in Engineering; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for both 642 and 643.
courses.prereq: 2010, CPHR 2.0 or higher, and rank 3 or 4 in Engineering; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Introduction to Composites
courses.description:
In this seven-week course, students will gain the theoretical background as well as practical knowledge of the structure and properties of ceramic, metal, and polymer matrix composites.
Prereq: 3261, or Grad standing, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 644 or 5711.
courses.prereq: 3261, or Grad standing, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Crystalline Solids at High Temperatures
courses.description:
Strength and deformation mechanisms in crystalline solids at high temperatures.
Prereq: 3261 or 3332; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 3261 or 3332; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Fracture and Fatigue of Engineering Materials
courses.description: This seven week course will provide a background in fracture and fatigue with a survey of material-specific mechanisms. Prereq: 3261, or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 5763.
courses.prereq: 3261, or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MATSCEN
courses.title: Corrosion
courses.description:
Introduction of basic principles underlying the electrochemical corrosion degradation of metals, role of corrosion in material failures, and experimental corrosion evaluation approaches. An understanding of the fundamental thermodynamics and kinetics of electrochemical corrosion processes will be developed and serve as scientific foundation for understanding these topics.
Prereq: Sr or Grad standing in Engineering, or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: Sr or Grad standing in Engineering, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Statics
courses.description:
Vector concepts of static equilibrium for isolated and connected bodies, centroids, inertia, truss, frame and machine analysis, and friction.
Prereq: Engr 1181 or 1187 or 1281H, and Physics 1250 or 1260, and Math 1151, 1140 or 1161. Not open to students with credit for 2010H or 2040.
courses.prereq: Engr 1181 or 1187 or 1281H, and Physics 1250 or 1260, and Math 1151, 1140 or 1161

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Statics
courses.description:
Vector concepts of static equilibrium for isolated and connected bodies, centroids, inertia, truss, frame and machine analysis, friction and virtual work.
Prereq: Honors standing, and Engr 1181 or 1187 or 1281H, and Physics 1250 or 1260, and Math 1151, 1140 or 1161. Not open to students with credit for 2010 or 2040.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and Engr 1181 or 1187 or 1281H, and Physics 1250 or 1260, and Math 1151, 1140 or 1161

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Mechanics of Materials
courses.description:
Stress and strain analysis of deformable structural components subjected to unidirectional and combined loads; pressure vessels; stress transformations (Mohr's Circle); beam deflections; column buckling.
Prereq: 2010, 2010H or 2040.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Dynamics
courses.description:
Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; linear and angular motion; work and energy; and single degree of freedom vibration analysis.
Prereq: 2010 or 2010H or 2040.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Statics and Introduction to Mechanics of Materials
courses.description:
Vector concepts of static equilibrium, truss, frame and machine analysis. Stress and strain analysis of deformable structural components; stress transformations; beam deflections; column buckling.
Prereq: Engr 1181 or 1187 or 1281H, and Physics 1250 or 1260, and Math 1152 or 1161 or 1172 or 1181H. Not open to students with credit for 2020.
courses.prereq: Engr 1181 or 1187 or 1281H, and Physics 1250 or 1260, and Math 1152 or 1161 or 1172 or 1181H

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Individual Studies in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Designed to give the advanced student opportunity to pursue special studies not otherwise offered. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 15 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description:
Numerical solutions of nonlinear equations, systems of linear equations, interpolation, curve-fitting, ordinary differential equations.
Prereq: 2010 or 2040; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: Math 2174, 2568, or 2415 or equiv.; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 2010 or 2040; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: Math 2174, 2568, or 2415 or equiv.; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Design in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description:
Introduction to the discipline of Mechanical Engineering through a structured design, build, and test sequence. Students will fabricate apparatus which requires a basic understanding of the full scope of Mechanical Engineering.
Prereq: 2010 and Physics 1251; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: MatScEn 2010; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 2010 and Physics 1251; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: MatScEn 2010; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: System Dynamics and Vibrations
courses.description:
Applications of ordinary differential equations, Laplace transforms, transfer function analysis to first and second order systems, and single-degree-of-freedom mechanical and electrical systems.
Prereq: 2850.xx and 2030; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: 2900; and ECE 2300 or 2300.01; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 2850.xx and 2030; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: 2900; and ECE 2300 or 2300.01; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: System Integration and Control
courses.description:
Modeling of a variety of multi-domain systems, including electromechanical actuators, principles of feedback control, and analysis of control systems.
Prereq: 3260; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or department permission. Prereq or concur: 3503, 2900, and ECE 2300.
courses.prereq: 3260; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or department permission

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Engineering Thermal Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and heat transfer with engineering applications. Prereq: Math 2174 or 2177 or 2255 (255) or 2415 (415), and Physics 1250 (131). Not open to students with credit for 500 or enrolled in MechEng major.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.description:
Principles of engineering thermodynamics from the classical perspective, including first and second laws of thermodynamics, with selected applications.
Prereq: Chem 1210 or 1250; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: 2850.xx; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: Chem 1210 or 1250; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: 2850.xx; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
courses.description:
A study of the basic concepts, fundamental equations, and applications of fluid mechanics to engineering problems.
Prereq: 2850.xx and 3501; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 2850.xx and 3501; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Design and Analysis of Machine Elements I
courses.description:
Design of mechanisms. Application of general mechanical engineering principles to the design and analysis of mechanical components.
Prereq: 2020, 2030, 2850 and MatScEn 2010; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 2020, 2030, 2850 and MatScEn 2010; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Design and Analysis of Machine Elements II
courses.description:
Continuation of 3670 and 3571.
Prereq: 3670 and 3751; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 3670 and 3751; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Kinematics and Mechanism Design
courses.description:
This course is intended to help students develop an intuitive understanding of the design concepts for machinery and mechanisms. Topics covered are: kinematic joints, mobility analysis, kinematic synthesis of planar linkages, computer-aided design of mechanisms, kinematic analysis, Cam motion program synthesis, and cam profile design.
Prereq: 2020, 2030, 2850.xx and MatScEn 2010; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 2020, 2030, 2850.xx and MatScEn 2010; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Measurements and Data Analysis in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description:
Foundation in experimental measurement and data analysis in mechanical engineering; team planning and execution of experiments; technical report writing.
Prereq: Stat 3450 or equiv; and GE Foundation Writing and Information Literacy course; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: 3503 and 2900; or permission of the department.
courses.prereq: Stat 3450 or equiv; and GE Foundation Writing and Information Literacy course; and enrollment as MechEng-BS student; Prereq or concur: 3503 and 2900; or permission of the department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Individual Studies in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description:
Designed to give the advanced student opportunity to pursue special studies not otherwise offered.
Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 15 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Individual Studies in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description:
Designed to give the advanced student opportunity to pursue special studies not otherwise offered.
Prereq: Permission of Instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 15 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of Instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Nuclear Science and Engineering
courses.description:
Discussion of nuclear energy and nuclear radiation; sources, methods of utilization, and projections for future engineering uses.
Prereq: Math 2153 or above and Physics 1251, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for NuclrEn 4505. Cross-listed in NuclrEn.
courses.prereq: Math 2153 or above and Physics 1251, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description:
A study of the fundamentals of conduction, convection, and thermal radiation energy transfer with engineering applications.
Prereq: 3503; and MechEng-BS student; or permission of department.
courses.prereq: 3503; and MechEng-BS student; or permission of department

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Automotive Manufacturing
courses.description:
This course is an introduction to automotive manufacturing as implemented in the certificate program at OSU in the College of Engineering.
Prereq: Engr 1182.01; or 1282.01H; or 1282.02H; or 1282.04H; or 1186.01, and 1187 and 1188; and enrollment in the College of Engineering. Not open to students with credit for ECE 4670, ISE 4610, WeldEng 4610. Cross-listed in ISE, WeldEng and ECE 4670.
courses.prereq: Engr 1182.01; or 1282.01H; or 1282.02H; or 1282.04H; or 1186.01, and 1187 and 1188; and enrollment in the College of Engineering

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Practical Experience in Automotive Manufacturing or Related Area
courses.description:
Practical experience in automotive manufacturing from a cooperative work experience, internship, undergraduate research project, capstone project, or participation on a student motorsports team.
Prereq: 4610; or ISE 4610; or WeldEng 4610; or ECE 4670. Not open to students with credit for ISE 4611, WeldEng 4611 or ECE 4671. Cross-listed in ISE 4611, WeldEng 4611 and ECE 4671.
courses.prereq: 4610; or ISE 4610; or WeldEng 4610; or ECE 4670

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Multidisciplinary Mechanical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description:
Builds upon prior laboratory experiences and integrates thermal and mechanical system concepts; focus on problem solving using experimental and analytical/computational methods.
Prereq: 3360, 3671, and 3870, and enrollment as MechEng-BS or EngPhys-BS student. Prereq or concur: 4510.
courses.prereq: 3360, 3671, and 3870, and enrollment as MechEng-BS or EngPhys-BS student

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: ME Capstone Design I: General Projects
courses.description:
First course of 2-semester capstone sequence. Students work on design problems proposed by faculty. Emphasis on problem definition, requirements, and design proposal.
Prereq: 3360, 3671, 3503 and 3870. Prereq or concur: 4510, and GenEd 1201 or GenEd 2601, and enrollment as a MechEng-BS Student, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: ME Capstone Design II: General Projects
courses.description:
Second course of 2-semester senior capstone series. Complete work on design problem proposed by faculty. Emphasis on detailed design, prototype, evaluation, and documentation.
Prereq: 4901.01; and GenEd 1201 or 2601.xx; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 4901.01; and GenEd 1201 or 2601.xx; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: ME Capstone Design I: Student Design Competitions
courses.description:
First course of 2-semester capstone sequence. Students work on design problems arising from various student competitions in engineering. Emphasis on problem definition, requirements, and design proposal.
Prereq: 3360, 3671, 3503, and 3870; and GenEd 1201 or 2601. Prereq or concur: 4510; and enrollment as a MechEng-BS Student; or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: ME Capstone Design II: Student Design Competitions
courses.description:
Second course of 2-semester senior capstone series. Complete work on design project associated with student design competitions. Emphasis on detailed design, prototype, evaluation, and documentation.
Prereq: 4902.01; and GenEd 1201 or 2601; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 4902.01; and GenEd 1201 or 2601; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: ME Capstone Design I: Product Design
courses.description:
First course of two-semester senior capstone series. Students begin to work on their design project. Emphasis on problem definition, requirements, design proposal.
Prereq: 3360, 3671, 3870, and GenEd 1201 or GenEd 2601. Prereq or concur: 4510 and 5682.01, and enrollment as a MechEng-BS Student; or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: ME Capstone Design II: Product Design Capstone
courses.description:
Second course of 2-semester senior capstone series. Complete work on design problem proposed by faculty. Emphasis on detailed design, prototype, evaluation, documentation.
Prereq: 4906.01, and enrollment as MechEng-BS Student (No MechEng pre-majors can enroll in this course); or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 4906.01, and enrollment as MechEng-BS Student (No MechEng pre-majors can enroll in this course); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Opportunity for undergraduate students to conduct research in Mechanical Engineering. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 6 cr hrs or 6 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description:
Opportunity for undergraduate Honors program students to conduct research in Mechanical Engineering.
Prereq: Honors standing, and enrollment in MechEng major, and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 6 cr hrs or 6 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and enrollment in MechEng major, and permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Undergraduate Research for Thesis
courses.description: Students are offered the opportunity to pursue independent project/research. Student presentations and undergraduate thesis writing is included. Prereq: CPHR 3.0 or above, and Sr standing in MechEng major; or permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 6 cr hrs or 4 completions.
courses.prereq: CPHR 3.0 or above, and Sr standing in MechEng major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Undergraduate Research for Thesis
courses.description: Honors program students are offered the opportunity to pursue independent project/research. Student presentations and undergraduate Honors thesis writing is included, to enable graduation with Research Distinction in Mechanical Engineering. Prereq: Honors standing, and CPHR 3.4 or above, and Sr standing in MechEng major; or permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 6 cr hrs or 4 completions.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and CPHR 3.4 or above, and Sr standing in MechEng major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Vibrations of Deformable Solids
courses.description: Introduction to the analysis of the free and forced transverse vibrations of strings, beams, membranes and plates and the longitudinal and torsional vibrations of prismatic bars. Prereq: 2020 (420) or 2040, and Math 2174, 2177, or 2415 (415), and enrollment in MechEng major; or Grad standing in MechEng. Not open to students with credit for 734.
courses.prereq: 2020 (420) or 2040, and Math 2174, 2177, or 2415 (415), and enrollment in MechEng major; or Grad standing in MechEng

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Applied Finite Element Method
courses.description:
Overview of finite element method, description of finite element software, modeling requirements and techniques, analysis using general purpose software, and case studies.
Prereq: 2020 or 2040 or equiv, and enrollment in MechEng major; or Grad standing in Engineering.
courses.prereq: 2020 or 2040 or equiv, and enrollment in MechEng major; or Grad standing in Engineering

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Engineering Fracture Mechanics
courses.description: Fracture and fatigue of solids; stress intensity factors; stability of cracks; compliance and energy methods; plane stress, plane strain effects; crack propagation and arrest criteria. Prereq: 2020 (420) or 2040, and Math 2174, 2177, or 2415 (415); or Grad standing in Engineering. Not open to students with credit for 744.
courses.prereq: 2020 (420) or 2040, and Math 2174, 2177, or 2415 (415); or Grad standing in Engineering

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Group Studies in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Special topics in Mechanical Engineering. The particular topic, credit hours, and the instructor will be announced the semester previous to the one in which the course is offered. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 10 cr hrs or 10 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Vehicle Dynamics
courses.description: A first course in vehicle dynamics devoted to the basic concepts of rubber wheeled vehicles with an actual driving and demonstrated laboratory. Prereq: 3360 (482) and 3671 (563), or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 654 or 754.
courses.prereq: 3360 (482) and 3671 (563), or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Mechanical Vibrations
courses.description:
Free and forced vibration analysis of single-degree-of-freedom systems with various forms of damping, vibration isolation and control methods and devices, vibration sensors, equations of motion of multi-degree of freedom systems using Lagrange's method, Eigen value problem, modal analysis method for free and forced vibration analysis, frequency-domain data analysis fundamentals.
Prereq: 3260 (481). Prereq or concur: 3360 (482), or Grad standing in Engineering. Not open to students with credit for 650, 666, or 7250.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Modeling and Simulation Techniques for Dynamic Systems and Control
courses.description:
Introduction and use of software tools for dynamic system modeling, control system analysis, and design. Application to real world dynamic systems, with emphasis on model development and validation, parameter identification, and results presentation.
Prereq: 3360; and enrollment in MechEng; or Graduate standing in MechEng; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 3360; and enrollment in MechEng; or Graduate standing in MechEng; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Theory and Applications of Feedback Control
courses.description:
Introduction to multi-domain (mechanical, thermal, fluid, electrical, electronic, electro-mechanical) system design, dynamic modeling, and control system design and analysis techniques.
Prereq: 3360 or 3361, or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 3360 or 3361, or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Smart Materials and Intelligent Systems
courses.description: Macromechanical modeling of smart materials including piezoceramics, magnetostrictives, shape memory alloys, magnetorheological fluids, and active polymers. Constitutive and system-level modeling. Design of smart dynamic systems. Prereq: 3360 (571) or 3361, or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 774.
courses.prereq: 3360 (571) or 3361, or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Introduction to Turbomachinery
courses.description: Introduction to analysis and design of turbomachinery. Prereq: 3503 or 3504 (504), or Grad standing in MechEng. Not open to students with credit for 627.
courses.prereq: 3503 or 3504 (504), or Grad standing in MechEng

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: Design and operating characteristics of contemporary internal combustion engines, induction/exhaust breathing, boosting, variable valvetrains, combustion and knock, fuel economy, alternative fuels, and advanced powertrains. Prereq: 3501 or 3502 (502), or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 630.
courses.prereq: 3501 or 3502 (502), or Grad standing in MechEng, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Applied Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer
courses.description: Introduces basic concepts in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Computational Heat Transfer (CHT), teaches thermo-fluid analysis of engineering systems, and enhances understanding of fluid flow and heat transfer. Prereq: 3501 or 3502 (502), and 3503 or 3504 (504). Prereq or concur: 4510 (510), or Grad standing in MechEng.

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Heating, Ventilating, and Air Conditioning
courses.description: Analysis of components and systems for heating, ventilating and air-conditioning. Prereq: 4510 (510), or Grad standing in MechEng. Not open to students with credit for 641.
courses.prereq: 4510 (510), or Grad standing in MechEng

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing
courses.description: Design of machine components, surfaces, and assemblies using parametric and feature-based design principles and advanced design tools. Prereq: 3670 (561), or Grad standing in Engineering, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 621 or 683.
courses.prereq: 3670 (561), or Grad standing in Engineering, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Fundamentals of Product Design Engineering
courses.description:
Lecture covering the fundamentals of the product design process, from concept creation to final implementation, including product architecture and design for manufacture and assembly. Only open to students enrolled in majors in the College of Engineering.
Prereq: Jr, Sr, or Grad standing in the College of Engineering, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 5682.02.
courses.prereq: Jr, Sr, or Grad standing in the College of Engineering, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: MECHENG
courses.title: Study at a Foreign Institution
courses.description: An opportunity for students to study at a foreign institution and receive Ohio State credit for that work. Prereq: Permission of department chairperson. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 2 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of department chairperson

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Individual Studies in Nuclear Engineering
courses.description: Designed to give the advanced student opportunity to pursue special studies not otherwise offered. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 4 cr hrs or 4 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Individual Studies in Nuclear Engineering
courses.description: Designed to give the advanced student opportunity to pursue special studies not otherwise offered. Prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 4 cr hrs or 4 completions.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Introduction to Nuclear Science and Engineering
courses.description:
Discussion of nuclear energy and nuclear radiation; sources, methods of utilization, and projections for future engineering uses.
Prereq: Math 2153 or above and Physics 1251, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for MechEng 4505. Cross-listed in MechEng.
courses.prereq: Math 2153 or above and Physics 1251, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Undergraduate Nuclear Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: A laboratory course tailored to undergraduates that will provide hands-on experience with nuclear engineering instrumentation and the OSU Research Reactor. Prereq: 4505 (505) or MechEng 4505 (505); or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 4505 (505) or MechEng 4505 (505); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Nuclear Reactor Systems
courses.description: Introductory course covering concepts of nuclear power reactor systems, thermal and mechanical design aspects and economics of nuclear power plants. Prereq: 4505 (505) or MechEng 4505 (505); or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 6536 (736), MechEng 4536 or 6536 (736). Cross-listed in MechEng.
courses.prereq: 4505 (505) or MechEng 4505 (505); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Nuclear Engineering
courses.description: Designed to give the advanced student opportunity to pursue special studies not otherwise offered.  Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 10 cr hrs or 10 completions. This course is graded S/U.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Nuclear Engineering
courses.description: Designed to give the advanced student opportunity to pursue special studies not otherwise offered. Prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 10 cr hrs or 10 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Radiation Protection and Shielding
courses.description: General principles of radiation, radioactivity, and radiation protection including radiation sources, radioactive decay, radiation interactions, radiation detection, radiation shielding, radiation dose calculations, and biological effects. Prereq: Math 2153, 2173, 2177 or 153, and Physics 1250 or 133; or Grad standing. Not open to students with credit for 606.
courses.prereq: Math 2153, 2173, 2177 or 153, and Physics 1250 or 133; or Grad standing

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Reactor Safety
courses.description: Introductory course covering concepts of reactor safety, the history of reactor accidents and methods of safety analysis. Prereq: 4505 (505) or MechEng 4505 (505); or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 610.
courses.prereq: 4505 (505) or MechEng 4505 (505); or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: NUCLREN
courses.title: Nuclear Instrumentation, Radiation Sensor and Detection
courses.description: Systematic study of nuclear radiation source, interaction with matter and their detection using gas-filled, semiconductor, Scintillation detectors, HPGe spectrometry, pulse processing, and statistical data analysis.

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Introduction to Welding Engineering
courses.description:
Study of the principles of welding engineering, including processes, design, weldability of materials, codes and standards, and quality assurance.
Prereq: MatScEng 2010, Physics 1251, and WeldEng-BS student; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: MatScEng 2010, Physics 1251, and WeldEng-BS student; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Introductory Arc Welding Laboratory
courses.description:
Basic skills required for manual and semiautomatic arc welding processes.
Prereq: Chem 1210 or 1250; and Math 1151 or 1161; and Physics 1250 or 1260; and enrollment as WeldEng-BS major or pre-major student. Not open to students outside of WeldEng-BS major or pre-major.
courses.prereq: Chem 1210 or 1250; and Math 1151 or 1161; and Physics 1250 or 1260; and enrollment as WeldEng-BS major or pre-major student

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Individual Studies in Welding Engineering
courses.description: Investigations in areas of advanced non-thesis research. Library and/or research investigations under the directions of instructors. Comprehensive report required. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 12 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Physical Principles in Welding Processes I
courses.description:
Study of the application of physical principles in engineering of arc welding processes and equipment.
Prereq: 2001 or 3001, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major. Prereq or concur: ECE 2300; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2001 or 3001, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Physical Principles in Welding Processes II
courses.description:
Study of the application of physical principles in engineering of non-arc welding processes and equipment.
Prereq: 2001 or 3001, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major or MatScEn-BS major; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2001 or 3001, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major or MatScEn-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Resistance Welding Processes
courses.description: Addresses the fundamentals, theory, and application of Resistance Welding processes, with emphasis on processes, equipment, materials, and quality control. Prereq: 4002, and enrollment as WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 602 or 702.
courses.prereq: 4002, and enrollment as WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Brazing and Soldering
courses.description:
Brazing and soldering processes with emphasis on physical and metallurgical principles, materials, design and application considerations.
Prereq: 2001 or 3001 and MatScEn 2251, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS or MatSEng-BS major; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2001 or 3001 and MatScEn 2251, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS or MatSEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: High Energy Density Welding Processes
courses.description: Theory and practice of laser, electron beam, and other high energy density welding processes. Prereq: 4001, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS or MatScEn-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 704.
courses.prereq: 4001, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS or MatScEn-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Welding Metallurgy I
courses.description:
Application of physical metallurgy principles to nonequilibrium thermo-mechanical conditions associated with welding in structural alloys and focus on carbon steels. Includes welding metallurgy laboratories.
Prereq: MatScEn 2251 and 3141, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS or MatSEng-BS major. Not open to students with credit for 4611.
courses.prereq: MatScEn 2251 and 3141, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS or MatSEng-BS major

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Welding Metallurgy II
courses.description:
Addresses the welding metallurgy and weldability principles associated with stainless steels, nickel-base, aluminum-base, and titanium-base alloys and other nonferrous alloys. Includes laboratories.
Prereq: 4101, and enrollment as WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 4612.
courses.prereq: 4101, and enrollment as WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Weldability
courses.description: Teaches the basic concepts of weldability and focuses on failure mechanisms in welded construction. Failure phenomena that occur during fabrication, repair, and during service are discussed. Prereq: 4101, and WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 714 or 715.
courses.prereq: 4101, and WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Computational Modeling of Additive Manufacturing and Welding
courses.description:
Fundamentals and applications of numerical methods for modeling additive manufacturing and welding processes and materials.
Prereq: Jr or Sr standing in WeldEng-BS major, or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: Jr or Sr standing in WeldEng-BS major, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Industrial Experience
courses.description: Experience in an industrial organization and the submitting of an acceptable report on the work done. Prereq: 4002 and 4202, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 489.
courses.prereq: 4002 and 4202, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Individual Studies in Welding Engineering
courses.description: Non-thesis research investigations under the directions of instructors. Comprehensive report required. Prereq: Enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major or MatScEn-BS major; and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 12 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major or MatScEn-BS major; and permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Engineering Analysis for Design and Simulation
courses.description:
Fundamentals of engineering analysis of heat flow, thermal and residual stresses, and fracture and fatigue with applications to design and simulation in welding and manufacturing.
Prereq: 2001 or 3001; and Math 2177, or 2255, or 2415, or 2174; and MechEng 2040 or 2020; and Engr 1221 or 1281H; and enrollment in WeldEng major; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2001 or 3001; and Math 2177, or 2255, or 2415, or 2174; and MechEng 2040 or 2020; and Engr 1221 or 1281H; and enrollment in WeldEng major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Welding Design
courses.description: Fundamentals of design and application of codes and standards for welded structures. Prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 621 or 641.
courses.prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Fitness-for-Service of Welded Structures
courses.description: The interrelationship of design, fabrication, nondestructive evaluation, fracture mechanics, and reliability concepts in establishing the overall fitness-for-purpose of welded structures. Prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 740.
courses.prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Nondestructive Evaluation
courses.description: Main concepts of Nondestructive Evaluation of materials as applied to inspections of joints and structures; principles of conventional methods and their capabilities and limitations. Prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 631.
courses.prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Welding of Plastics and Composites
courses.description: Theory and practice in welding of plastics and polymeric composites, including theory and analysis of welding processes, part and joint design, and process selection. Prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 706.
courses.prereq: 4201, and enrollment as a WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Topics in Welding Engineering
courses.description:
Theory and application of novel and hybrid welding processes.
Prereq: 2001, or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2001, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Welding Procedure Development and Qualification
courses.description:
This course is an introduction to developing and qualifying weld procedures and personnel to welding codes and standards (e.g., AWS B2.1). Hands on welding is required to qualify welding procedure specifications through weld testing for producing procedure qualification records. Weld inspection and acceptance criteria are also explored on how they affect weld design based on welding codes.
Prereq: 2001; and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2001; and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Welding Robot Programming and Operations
courses.description:
Laboratory experience programming and operation of robotic welding systems.
Prereq: 2001 or 3001, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 2001 or 3001, and enrollment in the WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Introduction to Automotive Manufacturing
courses.description:
This course is an introduction to automotive manufacturing as implemented in the certificate program at OSU in the College of Engineering.
Prereq: Engr 1181.xx and 1182.xx, or ENGR 1281.xx and 1282.xx, or ENGR 1186.xx and 1187 and 1188; and enrollment in the College of Engineering. Not open to students with credit for ECE 4670, ISE 4610, or MechEng 4610. Cross-listed in ISE, MechEng and ECE 4670.
courses.prereq: Engr 1181.xx and 1182.xx, or ENGR 1281.xx and 1282.xx, or ENGR 1186.xx and 1187 and 1188; and enrollment in the College of Engineering

courses.description:
Practical experience in automotive manufacturing from a cooperative work experience, internship, undergraduate research project, capstone project, or participation on a student motorsports team.
Prereq: 4610; or ISE 4610; or MechEng 4610; or ECE 4670. Not open to students with credit for ISE 4611, MechEng 4611 or ECE 4671. Cross-listed in ISE 4611, MechEng 4611 and ECE 4671.
courses.prereq: 4610; or ISE 4610; or MechEng 4610; or ECE 4670

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Capstone Welding Design I

Group design projects building on all aspects of Welding Engineering.

courses.prereq: GedEd 1201 or 2601, and Sr standing in WeldEng-BS major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: WELDENG
courses.title: Capstone Welding Design II

Group design projects building on all aspects of Welding Engineering.
